toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
What is going on: the Kestria buffering is not caused by the Tessaline CDN. The same Tessaline delivery serves web, iOS/Android and smart-TV 5.1 (auto-update off) with rebuffering around 0.6–0.7%, the same as before. Only smart-TV app 5.2, released on 9 October, sits at about 5.9%, and it shows that rate on every ISP. Its start-up time is also slower in a way that fits a new adaptive-streaming setup. The timing matches: the rise began on 9 October, the day 5.2 went live. The handball launch does not explain it, since the rise came before it and the match nights are flat.

How sure: fairly sure about the pattern (about 85%). The exact mechanism inside 5.2 is not yet confirmed.

What to do next: revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming settings in Kestria to the 5.1 behaviour and pause the wider 5.2 rollout until fixed. Do not approve the Tessaline breach notice, the fee withholding or the move back to Corvane, since they target the wrong cause. Keep the Kestria rebuffering alert on, and add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard, although that needs a pipeline rebuild that is about six weeks away. Treat the cancellation link as unproven before offering refunds.
output.methodChoice: Collected one item (X10), the playback breakdown by app, version and ISP, which discriminated between the CDN and app-release explanations.
